_comment: PRD §6/§10/§18. temporal_mode and measured_fps are written by scripts/probe_cameras.py at 17:45-18:00 and must match what the UI displays (AC-15). Zone polygons are [[x,y],...] in image pixel space, calibrated manually per camera (§10) - no automatic intersection understanding.
_fps_basis: Measured by scripts/probe_cameras.py (image-hash comparison, 60 samples/camera). All three ladder cameras land at 0.50-0.51 fps / ~2.0s, so this one figure is honest for every rung: CPW@86 0.500 (31 frames), Exterior@3Ave 0.511 (32), Canal@Chrystie 0.509 (32). The ~2s refresh is a property of the NYCTMC platform, not of one camera.
_temporal_mode_basis: Revised from 'frames' to 'cooccupancy' (Variant C) per ADR-008. The ByteTrack harness (scripts/test_feed.py) found the live feed is 352x240 at night in rain, putting VRUs at ~12-20px tall - under the ~25px recall floor PRD §9 flags - which makes ID churn likely at 0.5 fps regardless of tracker tuning. §26's fallback rung, taken proactively rather than after a live PASS/FAIL run that credentials do not yet exist to perform.

cameras.intersection: Central Park West & W 86 St, Manhattan

context.facility_type: painted bike lane on Central Park West, visible in camera frame
context.source: NYC Open Data: Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95) + New York City Truck Routes (jjja-shxy)
context.query: within_circle(location, 40.785302, -73.969353, 250) AND crash_date >= '2021-08-07' AND (number_of_cyclist_injured > 0 OR number_of_pedestrians_injured > 0)

demo_replay._comment: Mandatory rung (§18). Prerecorded input, not prerecorded inference - runs through the same Roboflow pipeline (AC-10). Capture by 19:35.

_zone_basis: Polygons are [[x,y],...] in 352x240 image pixel space, hand-calibrated by eye against demo/frames/frame_01.jpg (PRD §10 - manual, no homography, no automatic intersection understanding). Test point is the bbox bottom-centre. These are eyeballed from a single night frame and are the least precise part of the system.
